extracted.intended_audience: USPTO policymakers, patent examiners, and patent practitioners (applicants/attorneys)
extracted.subtask_description: Standards, procedural recommendations, and measurable metrics for improving patent examination quality, prosecution practice, and USPTO administrative processes. Covers RCE handling, reasons for allowance, application formatting and content, data collection and transparency, examiner incentives, and outcome/result metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCE handling — maintain same examiner
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain same examiner on RCE as original.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendation to avoid changing examiner on a Request for Continued Examination (RCE) to preserve continuity of prosecution and reduce unnecessary repeat work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purgatory RCEs — remain unexamined until request
rubrics_metrics.description: RCE to remain unexamined until applicant pays fee and requests continued prosecution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposal that RCEs should not be automatically examined; they could wait in 'purgatory' until the applicant affirmatively requests continued prosecution and pays the fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gather root causes of RCEs
rubrics_metrics.description: Gather information on the 'root causes' of RCEs to address varied issues rather than a one‐size‐fits‐all procedure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use data on why RCEs are filed (e.g., solely to cite new prior art, no claim amendments) to devise expedited or alternative resolution paths for RCEs not presenting substantive amendments or arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expedited path for non-amendment RCEs
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide an expedited or alternative path for RCEs that are not filed to present claim amendments or additional arguments for patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include RCEs filed only to add prior art citations or to comply with Rule 56; consider special fast-track procedures for such RCEs.

rubrics_metrics.name: No production credit for minimal-work RCEs
rubrics_metrics.description: If there is little or no work needed to allow a case on an RCE, no production credit should be given to the examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure amount of examiner work by character of amendments after RCE; if amendments are minimal and could have been considered earlier, production credit should be withheld to remove incentive to push cases into needless RCEs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant responsibility to present clear claims early
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants have a shared responsibility to reduce unnecessary continuations by presenting clear claims that capture the invention early in the process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incentives (e.g., fees increasing with number of continuing applications) could encourage clearer early claim drafting without eliminating the right to continue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasons for allowance — comprehensive and clear
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiner’s statement of reasons for allowance should be comprehensive and clear.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reasons for allowance should not introduce unsupported claim limitations or broadening language not of record; should make the basis for allowance transparent to patentee and public (MPEP 1302.14).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasons for allowance — identify distinguishing claim elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiner should identify claim elements or how combination thereof distinguish claimed invention over prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain specifically what elements or combinations provide novelty/obviousness distinction so scope and basis are explicit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify priority date for claim elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify priority date for each claim element in continuing and continuation-in-part applications: which supported by original application, which have later effective date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly state which claim elements derive benefit of earlier filings to avoid later ambiguity.

rubrics_metrics.name: State interpretation of claim preamble and functional terms
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiner should state the interpretation given in prosecution to claim preamble and any field of use or functional terminology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If preamble not relied upon by examiner, that should be stated so patentee and public know how to interpret claim scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify file history estoppel and basis for allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: Identification of file history estoppel: examiner should indicate claim amendments and arguments presented by applicant (e.g. disclaimers, admissions) which formed the basis for allowance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose is to eliminate subsequent uncertainty about claim scope and provide a clear record of concessions or limiting arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continue to review allowance decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Continue internal review of allowance to ensure reasons for allowance are sound and aligned with goal of valid, clear claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Post-allowance review should check record, reasons, and conformity with quality objectives (internal Quality Review suggested).

rubrics_metrics.name: Means-plus-function in software — link function to structure
rubrics_metrics.description: For software and other patents relying on 112(6) 'means plus function' claiming, attempt to link the function recited in the claim with structure recited in the specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Merely identifying such linkage could assist the examiner; failure may indicate need for stronger linking language or missing structure in specification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expedite reexaminations
rubrics_metrics.description: Reexaminations should be expedited; impose a strictly observed, accelerated reexamination schedule (e.g., finish in one year).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reexamination often takes as long or longer than regular examination despite much prior art/search work having been done; faster schedules would preserve patent value and incentivize innovation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accelerated examination incentives for higher-quality applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide accelerated examination incentive for applicants who file higher-quality applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage applicants to submit better-prepared initial filings to reduce pendency and rework.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide application checklists and high-quality samples by art unit
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare application checklist for applicants, and provide samples of high quality applications in each art unit as best practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make examples and templates available so practitioners know what constitutes a high-quality submission in each technology area.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characteristics of high-quality applications
rubrics_metrics.description: High quality applications examples: applications with defined terms, 30 pages or less of specification, examples that support claim limitations, 10 or fewer claims and IDS, and request for first office action interview.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a proposed template for what qualifies for accelerated processing or considered high quality by the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide sample claim templates per art unit
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide examples of high-quality patent applications and sample claim formats for each art group unit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publishing claim templates helps practitioners craft claims using techniques specific to an art unit and helps align expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant as lexicographer — define terms in specification
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant is entitled to be his own lexicographer: provide definitions of terms in specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When definitions are present, examiner should refer to them; absence of definitions increases probability of misunderstanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use standard dictionaries or agreed third-party dictionary when undefined
rubrics_metrics.description: In the absence of definitions, use standard dictionaries or adopt a mutual third-party dictionary selection process (IBM proposal).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A mutually agreed independent dictionary would aid claim interpretation and 112 determinations concerning disclosure adequacy and clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner should specify claim term definitions and sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim construction: examiner should specify the definition of terms relied upon in prior art and applicant's claim and source of that claim construction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly recording sources for claim term definitions improves transparency and reduces ambiguity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt common (trilateral) application format and document structuring
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt trilateral common format application: automatic line numbering, paragraph numbering starting with [0001], 4-character hard space, Arial font, page and paragraph numbering, 8.5x11 or A4, consistent margins and drawing scale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rigorous adherence to a standard format aids examiner comprehension, comparison of drawings, electronic handling, and uniformity across jurisdictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide bookmarks, high-quality images, and press-quality submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Use bookmarks/destinations and press quality images (at least 4000dpi) and electronic format to facilitate examiner review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow efficient navigation between figures (e.g., compare FIGs) and avoid scanning artifacts; drawings integrated with specification preferred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improve drawing formats — enable zooming, color, vector, video
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings should not be static 8.5x11 black and white images; allow formats that support color, gray scale, zooming, panning, vector graphics, video, etc., and integrate drawings with the specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should provide electronic drawings to avoid PTO scanning and associated errors; charging for hard-copy-only submissions is suggested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard algorithm descriptive language for software filings
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants should be required to utilize standard algorithm descriptive language when source code is not disclosed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standardized descriptive language would aid search, examination and claim construction in computer science/software fields; propose compiling algorithms into a searchable database for reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjust count system to reflect complexity
rubrics_metrics.description: Count system should be adjusted (or replaced) so that it provides a more robust measurement of examiner productivity and recognizes application complexity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give greater credit for complex/lengthy applications, many claims, many prior art references; avoid perverse incentives (e.g., issuing restriction requirements to get multiple counts).

rubrics_metrics.name: Docket visibility and timely examiner communication
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners should return applicant’s telephone call within 24 hours and ensure same-day responses are properly entered; respond to applicant status inquiries within 3 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Improve transparency and communication channels between examiners and applicants; ensure prompt entry of communications into the file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use revision controls (track changes) for responses
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of track change software for all responses to make it easier to see where and when changes and amendments are made; front end interface to file history.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Facilitates review by examiners, applicants, and quality reviewers to understand edits over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submit applications electronically (XML) and improve electronic tracking
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit all applications electronically in XML format and use electronic tracking (bar codes) to determine location of all documents to eliminate misplaced files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Integrate filing, docketing, searching and office action correspondence so processes are not siloed (EFS-Web, eDAN, EAST, OACS integration suggested).

rubrics_metrics.name: Remove requirement to submit USPTO-generated patents/publications in IDS
rubrics_metrics.description: Remove requirement to submit U.S. Patents and Published U.S. Patent Applications in IDS's, especially those already in USPTO databases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instead, allow cross-referencing electronically to documents already housed by PTO to avoid duplicate submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow linkage to related cases and prosecution histories
rubrics_metrics.description: Allow applicant to identify/link to related cases (US or foreign) that have prosecution histories of possible interest to the examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Electronic linking to related prosecution histories can improve examiner understanding and avoid redundant submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make PTO website electronic copy the 'official' copy
rubrics_metrics.description: Electronic copy of the patent as shown on the PTO website should be the 'official' copy with accurate searchable text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fix OCR errors and support non-text objects (equations, tables) so that the PTO-hosted copy can be relied upon as authoritative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automatic appeal docketing when Reply Brief submitted
rubrics_metrics.description: Automatically and instantaneously docket Appeals to Board when Reply Brief submitted; clerk-review for form only and quickly (within a week).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid 6-12 month delays between Reply Brief and appeal docketing; consider auto-generated entry/docketing notices similar to other automated processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stale case review — SPE oversight
rubrics_metrics.description: Adherence to MPEP 707.02: any application pending for more than 5 years or up for a third action should always be reviewed by a SPE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Periodic supervisory review for long-pending or repeatedly-actioned cases to reduce undue pendency and identify systemic problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid hypertechnical OIPE practices that delay prosecution
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid hypertechnical application of policy by the OIPE that creates delays (e.g., refusing declarations for minor address corrections without initials).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical acceptance of minor corrections avoids unnecessary petitions and pendency increases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improve scanner quality to avoid Notices to File Corrected Applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Improved scanner quality for new applications—especially drawings—should be used to avoid Notices to File Corrected Application Papers required due to scanning artifacts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High-quality, dedicated scanners and maintenance reduce applicant costs and avoid delays prior to examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public data transparency — publish raw PTO data and quality metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Make entirety of PTO official data available to public in raw form and make certain quality metrics available to public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public, raw data supports objective, reproducible assessments of patent quality and allows collaborative metric development by stakeholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publish Office Actions evaluated and QA scoring sheets
rubrics_metrics.description: Make available the Office Actions that were evaluated and the scoring and evaluation sheets that were developed in response, and applications called back by Allowance Quality Review and following Action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transparency of reviewed cases and QA materials aids public understanding and reproducibility of quality assessments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publish pendency and QA results by Art Unit and customer number
rubrics_metrics.description: Regularly publish, by Group Art Unit (and by every entity having a customer number), the start date and filing date of the oldest pending application at each stage of the prosecution process and QA review results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include percentage of claims which were allowed and shouldn't have been, and percentage of claims which weren't allowed and should have been.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use third-party/software to compile and analyze quality data
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider use of third party and software to compile and analyze data; define scope of analysis and use raw data initially.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect raw per-application data first (not only derived metrics) to preserve degrees of freedom; select representative samples across Technology Centers and Art Units; consider external independent body for analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collect specified application-level data elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Collect data regarding the application as filed: number of dependent and independent claims, whether an IDS was initially filed, how many references cited broken down by type (US patents, non-US patents, non-patent prior art).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gather raw elements that enable derivation of various quality metrics and correlation analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collect applicant/inventor/assignee metadata
rubrics_metrics.description: Collect inventor, applicant, assignee information, including size (small/large entity, independent inventor, university), number of inventors, joint owners, assignees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows analysis of quality and outcomes by filer type and targeted policy interventions (e.g., small entity pilots).

rubrics_metrics.name: Collect counterpart/continuation family information
rubrics_metrics.description: Collect counterpart and continuation application information, including priority and family members identified as continuations, divisionals, continuations-in-part, RCEs, provisionals, PCTs and national applications, and information on any patents issuing thereon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Family-level data helps analyze continuation behavior, RCE frequency, and overall prosecution strategies/outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Track office actions, rejections by basis and correlated outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Track number of office actions per application, number of rejections therein broken down by basis (obviousness, written description, etc.) and correlate to outcome (amendment/cancellation of claims, abandonment, RCE filing, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enables identification of problematic rejection types and their downstream effects on pendency and allowances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure applicant responses and claim amendment types
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of applicant responses, including number of claim amendments and type (canceling, amending, or adding claims).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Helps understand prosecution dynamics (how many substantive amendments are occurring) and measure examiner workload appropriately (e.g., counts per claims examined).

rubrics_metrics.name: Count claims examined rather than case disposals
rubrics_metrics.description: Use claims examined rather than case disposals as a unit of examiner counts (e.g., one count per twenty claims examined).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Better aligns credit with actual substantive work rather than per-case counting that ignores claim volume/complexity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correlate key claim terms to specification definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Correlation of key claim terms to definition or description in the specification for applications as filed, issued patents, and terms added by claim amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess how closely claims map to specification disclosure; claims 'closer' to the specification are statistically more likely to be valid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collect appellate and pre-appeal practice metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Collect data on appellate practice such as pre-appeal conference statistics (allowance, reopening prosecution), basis for decisions on appeal (obviousness, written description, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use appellate outcomes to evaluate examination quality and refine training/QA practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure prosecution duration and pendency breakdowns
rubrics_metrics.description: Duration of prosecution measured from filing and/or first office action to issuance, with pendency broken down for original and any continuing applications, RCEs, appeals, interferences, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Time-based metrics by category help target pendency-improvement efforts and evaluate program impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent term adjustments printed on office actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent term adjustments maintained in real time and printed on every Office Action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide visibility into term adjustments throughout prosecution and increase transparency to applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stages of monitoring and review — stage-specific metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Monitor quality metrics at specified stages of prosecution: (1) when application is filed, (2) when initial search completed, (3) when first Office Action completed, (4) when an interview conducted, (5) when a reply to any non-final Office Action filed, (6) when an Office Action (non-final or final) or notice of allowance in response to a reply has been completed, (7) when an after-final submission filed, (8) when an appeal brief or other appeal-related paper filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stage-based monitoring allows feedback at critical junctures (e.g., early-review comments to applicant and examiner) to improve quality and reduce avoidable pendency.

rubrics_metrics.name: False negative error metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure false negative error metrics on a per-application and per-working-group basis: e.g., sample size; how many prima facie claim rejections were overcome without claim amendments; how many claim rejections overturned by primary examiners, SPEs/QAS, pre-appeal, appeal, reversed by courts; how many rejections presented again in subsequent Office Actions; how many subsequent searches were performed without new claims; identify examiner 'hot spots' with higher than average false negatives (+1 SD, +2 SD).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed breakdowns of overturned rejections at various levels identify systemic problems and training/QA targets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggregated quality metrics (per X applications)
rubrics_metrics.description: Aggregate metrics (e.g., per 1000 applications) for each measured working group: improper final rejections made; improper prima facie rejections; cases reopened after filing an appeal brief; applications opened after a pre-appeal conference; applications allowed after a pre-appeal conference; allowance rate per year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aggregate statistics enable cross-group comparisons and tracking of trends over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures for analysis, implementation, and communication
rubrics_metrics.description: Analyze metrics throughout each bi-week, consider independent external body for collection/analysis, promptly correct identified errors, develop positive incentives and recognition for reducing errors, report results publicly and timely, track 'lessons learned' to refine analyses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Continuous, iterative processes and external review reduce bias and ensure improvements are institutionalized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrate administrative software systems
rubrics_metrics.description: Integrate filing, docketing, searching, and office action correspondence to allow the USPTO to focus on substantive examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eliminate silos (EFS-Web, eDAN, EAST, OACS) to reduce resource waste and distraction from examination mission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transform static search templates into collaborative platform
rubrics_metrics.description: Transform PTO search template collection into a dynamic collaborative platform (e.g., wiki) to improve content and obtain third-party feedback.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Community-driven updates could add niche sources and improve templates used for Accelerated Examination searches and other searching activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Result metrics — track claim outcomes at trial
rubrics_metrics.description: Ultimate result metrics: outcome of claims at trial — validity upheld/reversed along with rationale (anticipation, obviousness, indefiniteness, inadequate description, non-enablement, claim construction issues, lack of antecedent basis, problems with means-plus-function support).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Linking prosecution/examination quality to trial outcomes provides the strongest measure of long-term patent quality and validity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Quality Index (PQI) — composite metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop composite metrics (Patent Quality Index) evaluating characteristics tied to validity: strength/accuracy of applicant and examiner search, sufficiency of support in specification for claims, effectiveness of office actions, closeness of claims to specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use statistical analysis to identify characteristics associated with validity and optimize procurement processes; claims 'closer' to the specification tend to be more likely valid.
